comparison: Both evaluate core NMJ denervation findings (C3, C4, C39-C42) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative data quality with appropriate statistics, while peer reviewers acknowledge these as key strengths demonstrating EOM sparing in ALS. Complete agreement on validity of these central observations.

Both evaluate satellite cell preservation findings (C5, C47-C49) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the parallel between SC depletion and NMJ denervation, while peer reviewers accept the differential preservation without challenge. Strong concordance on these observations.

Both evaluate FACS profiling of SC populations (C7, C8, C53-C58) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes some speculation in interpretation of Vcam1 heterogeneity, while peer reviewers praise the successful isolation and characterization. Agreement on data quality despite OpenEval's minor interpretive caution.

Both evaluate fusion index and renewability findings (C60-C65) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval and peer reviewers both accept the interpretation that low fusion reflects superior renewability. Peer review also includes broader claims about EOM SC properties (C9, C10, C89, C136). Strong agreement on these functional characterizations.

Major divergence on NaBu treatment effects (C13, C43, C44, C50). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on quantitative data showing improvements, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to editor's concern about NaBu's pleiotropic effects. Both acknowledge the data but differ on confidence in mechanistic interpretation.

Divergence on NaBu effects on differentiation (C67-C74, with overlap on C70-C73). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on dose-response and statistical analysis, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to concerns about NaBu's multiple biological effects. Data accepted but interpretation questioned by peers.

Perfect claim overlap (C93-C99) but divergent evaluations. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting honest reporting of mixed effects on stemness. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, citing editor's concerns about NaBu's pleiotropic actions. Both acknowledge the data but differ on confidence in mechanistic conclusions.

Both evaluate RNA-Seq analysis as SUPPORTED. OpenEval covers PCA/clustering (C75-C78) while peer review emphasizes successful transcriptomic comparison (C75, C76, C79-C81, C83, C84, C86-C88, C90-C92). Agreement on technical quality and validity of transcriptomic findings.

Both evaluate EOM SC transcriptomic signatures (C79-C85) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate differential expression criteria and reasonable speculation about BMP4. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of successful transcriptomic characterization. Strong concordance.

Both evaluate stemness signature analysis (C86-C92) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the functional interpretation about renewability preservation, while peer reviewers accept the transcriptomic comparison. Agreement on validity of signature gene analysis.

Both evaluate Cxcl12 identification (C100-C104) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes convergent identification across comparisons and reasonable speculation about shared mechanism. Peer reviewers praise identification of specific factors from transcriptomes. Strong agreement on this key finding.

Both evaluate qRT-PCR validation of Cxcl12 (C105-C113) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes independent validation strengthening RNA-Seq confidence. Peer reviewers accept Cxcl12 identification as impressive result. Agreement on validation quality, though peer review groups with broader transcriptomic findings.

Both evaluate AAV-Cxcl12 overexpression experiments (C114-C123) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes dramatic enhancement with strong statistics but mentions cross-species limitation. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge AAV-Cxcl12 experiments were addressed and provide impressive insights. Strong concordance despite OpenEval noting methodological limitation.

Both evaluate co-culture neurite extension findings (C118-C120) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative measurements and edge effect novelty. Peer reviewers accept demonstration of enhanced axon extensions. Agreement on functional validation of axon attraction properties.

Both evaluate uni-compartmental co-culture findings (C124-C130) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed quantification and notes multi-innervation phenotype with supporting molecular correlates. Peer reviewers accept enhanced innervation capabilities. Strong agreement on these functional observations.

Partial overlap on co-culture claims (C124-C126). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes innervation ratio quantification, while peer review focuses on AAV-Cxcl12 aspects. Agreement on validity of co-culture experimental approach.

Both evaluate background claims about ALS and neuromuscular disorders (C1, C2, C16-C21) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are well-established facts with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers accept foundational premises without question. Complete agreement on background context.

Both evaluate background literature on EOM properties (C22-C38) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations establishing rationale. Peer reviewers accept the premise about EOM preservation. Agreement on contextual background, though peer review covers fewer specific claims.

Divergence on interpretive/mechanistic claims (C131-C140). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, viewing these as reasonable synthesis with appropriate speculation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, citing need for further investigation of mechanisms. Both accept observations but differ on confidence in causal interpretations.

Partial overlap on NaBu mechanism claims (C154-C155). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, viewing synthesis with literature as appropriate. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to concerns about NaBu's multiple effects. Divergence reflects different confidence levels in mechanistic conclusions.

Both address Cxcl12 mechanism claims (C142-C148). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting accurate representation of literature with reasonable speculation about synergistic effects. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN for mechanistic interpretations generally. Partial divergence on confidence in proposed mechanisms.

OpenEval rates C141 (speculation about EOM vulnerability in oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy) as UNCERTAIN, noting it's purely speculative without supporting data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this tangential speculation.

OpenEval rates C158 (Relyvrio approval) as SUPPORTED factual statement providing clinical context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers did not specifically address this contextual claim.
